evidence: Source reads/edits and cached Java class data decoded as bytes only; no builds, tests, syntax checks, class loading, helper/project/game execution, GPU commands or Bedrock launch

reference.memoizeFunction: Util.memoize(Function) creates Util$10, whose ConcurrentHashMap cache uses computeIfAbsent(argument,function)
reference.memoizeBiFunction: Util.memoize(BiFunction) creates Util$11, whose ConcurrentHashMap cache uses Pair.of(first,second) and computeIfAbsent
reference.wrappers: RenderTypes.entitySolid(texture) and armorCutoutNoCull(texture) invoke distinct function caches. One-argument entityTranslucent and entityTranslucentEmissive delegate to their separate BiFunction caches with Boolean.TRUE.
reference.objectIdentity: RenderType has no equals/hashCode override in the cached method table. Its reference identity is distinct from PreparedRenderType record equality.
reference.preparedEquality: RenderType.prepare constructs PreparedRenderType from pipeline, outputTarget, dynamicTransforms GpuBufferSlice, copied ScissorState and prepared texture-binding list. Matching names or pixel buffers alone do not establish those five fields.
reference.phaseOrder: SubmitNodeStorage stores order collections in Int2ObjectAVLTreeMap; default custom geometry uses order 0, while Arctic emissive custom submits use order 1. Complete feature sorting/delivery remains separate from factory references.

port.class: JavaRenderType owns immutable factory, logical texture key and positive reference ID. Four caches implement only the selected one-argument factories, with Boolean.TRUE implicit for the two translucent families.
port.roles: Cosmetic base, explicit visible skin and bent skin share entityTranslucent's factory cache; glow uses entityTranslucentEmissive; cape uses entitySolid; wings use armorCutoutNoCull. GENERAL and anonymous texture inputs remain unknown.
port.bounds: Serialize admission across concurrent maps; retain existing reference objects without eviction or per-frame recycling. At most 65536 references across the four factories; exhaustion rejects new admission and fails staging rather than fabricating identity.
port.ownership: Reference objects and IDs belong to the source-port renderer, not the installed Java client's JVM. They reproduce supported factory argument reuse; they are neither native pointers, captured identity hashes, prepared GPU equality nor feature-phase ownership.
port.staging: NativeAvatarGeometry captures the selected immutable reference before texture/pixel staging; factory admission errors fail the builder transaction. Every Batch retains the reference independently of bitmap identity.
port.nativeValidation: Decoder validates factory/pass compatibility, positive bounded reference ID, required logical texture key and bidirectional consistency between reference and complete supported factory recipe. Plan.new rejects supplied render-object IDs that differ from a packet's known factory-cache reference. Prepared IDs, groups and sorting policy remain explicit separate inputs.

wire.magic: ARCGEO07 when any batch has a render reference; previous v6..v1 selection otherwise remains
wire.extension: After v5 logical texture metadata and before vertices, each v7 batch carries strict u8 presence; if 1, factory u8 and reference u64 little-endian
wire.budget: One byte for an unknown reference or ten for a known reference, included in the 96 MiB frame budget; at most 2048 batches
wire.compatibility: Rust retains ARCGEO01..06, with unknown references for older packets. V7 retains all earlier material, visibility, texture, actor, topology and pixel validation. No engine ABI or existing material flags change.
